p.src: Now, Aunt Xue had been so angered by J桂's outburst that her liver qi surged upward and her left side began to ache. Baochai knew perfectly well what had caused it. Unable even to wait for the doctor, she first sent someone to buy a few mace of gambir vine, had it brewed into a strong bowl of medicine, and gave it to her mother. Then she and Qiuling massaged Aunt Xue's legs and rubbed her chest. After a while, she felt somewhat more settled. Aunt Xue was torn between grief and anger: angry at J桂's outrageous behavior, and grieved that the patient and self-possessed Baochai should instead be the one deserving pity. Baochai soothed her for a while longer, and before she knew it Aunt Xue fell asleep. Her agitation gradually subsided as well. Baochai then said, “Mother, you must not take such pointless vexations to heart. In a few days, when you can walk again, you might as well go over to visit Grandmother and Aunt, have a talk with them, and relieve your spirits. Qiuling and I will be here to keep an eye on the house, and I doubt she will dare do anything.” Aunt Xue nodded. “We shall see in a day or two,” she said.

p.src: Meanwhile, after Imperial Consort Yuanchun recovered from her illness, everyone in the family rejoiced. Several days later, a number of palace eunuchs arrived with gifts and silver. They proclaimed Her Highness the Imperial Consort's command that everyone was to be rewarded for the diligence with which the family had inquired after her health. They handed over every item and sum of silver, accounting for each one clearly. Jia She, Jia Zheng, and the others reported the matter to Grandmother Jia, and after they had all given thanks for the imperial favor, the eunuchs drank some tea and departed. Everyone returned to Grandmother Jia's room and chatted and laughed for a while. An old serving-woman outside sent word in: “The pages report that someone over there is asking to see the Elder Master on urgent business.” Grandmother Jia said to Jia She, “You had better go.” Jia She assented, withdrew, and went on his way.

p.src: Grandmother Jia suddenly remembered something and said to Jia Zheng with a smile, “Her Highness truly keeps Baoyu in her thoughts. The other day she made a special point of asking after him.” Jia Zheng replied with a deferential smile, “But Baoyu is none too willing to study and so disappoints Her Highness's kind intentions.” “I put in a good word for him,” said Grandmother Jia. “I told her that his essays had improved of late.” Jia Zheng smiled. “He could hardly be as good as Your Ladyship says.” Grandmother Jia said, “You often have him go out to compose poems and essays. Surely he has managed to produce something. A child must be taught gradually. As the saying goes, ‘Even a fat man cannot grow fat on a single mouthful.’” At this, Jia Zheng hastily smiled in agreement. “Your Ladyship is quite right.” Grandmother Jia continued, “Speaking of Baoyu, there is another matter I want to discuss with you. He is grown now, and you ought to keep watch for a good girl and arrange a match for him. It is, after all, the great affair of his life. Never mind whether her kinship with us is close or distant, or whether she is poor or rich. It is enough that we know her disposition to be good and her looks pleasing and proper.” Jia Zheng said, “Your Ladyship's instructions are most sound. There is only one thing: the girl must indeed be good, but first he himself must learn to behave properly. Otherwise, if he amounts to nothing, he will merely blight another family's daughter. Would that not be a pity?” Grandmother Jia was somewhat displeased by this and said, “Strictly speaking, with you two here as his parents, there should be no need for me to concern myself. But Baoyu has been with me since childhood, and perhaps I have doted on him too much and delayed the serious business of raising him to manhood. Still, to my eyes he was born with decent looks and has an honest nature. Surely he is not necessarily such a hopeless creature that he must ruin another family's daughter. Perhaps I am partial, but however I look at it, he seems a little better than Huan. I wonder what all of you think.” These remarks made Jia Zheng deeply uneasy. He hurriedly replied with a deferential smile, “Your Ladyship has seen a great many people. Since you say he is good and destined for fortune, you are surely not mistaken. It is only that I have been too impatient to see him become a man. Perhaps, contrary to the ancient saying, I am one who ‘cannot perceive the beauty of his own son.’” This single remark teased Grandmother Jia into laughter, and everyone else joined in. Grandmother Jia then said, “You are getting on in years now, and you hold official office; naturally, experience has made you more mature and steady.” At this point she turned to Lady Xing and Lady Wang and said with a smile, “When he was young, what an eccentric temper he had! He was twice as peculiar as Baoyu.

p.src: It was only after he married that he began to understand a little about human ways. Now he does nothing but complain about Baoyu, yet to my mind Baoyu even now understands people's feelings a little better than he did then.” Her words made both Lady Xing and Lady Wang laugh. They said, “Your Ladyship has begun telling amusing stories again.” As they spoke, the young maids came in and said to Yuanyang, “Please inform Her Ladyship that the evening meal is ready to be served.” Grandmother Jia asked, “What are you whispering about over there?” Yuanyang smilingly explained the message to her. Grandmother Jia said, “In that case, all of you go and have your dinner. Only let Xifeng and Cousin Zhen's wife stay and eat with me.” Jia Zheng, Lady Xing, and Lady Wang all assented and waited while the meal was set out. Only after Grandmother Jia urged them once more did they withdraw and go their separate ways.

p.src: Lady Xing then went on her way. Jia Zheng and Lady Wang went into their room together. Referring to Grandmother Jia's words just now, Jia Zheng said, “Since Her Ladyship dotes on Baoyu so, he must acquire some genuine learning and later win a degree and official distinction. Only then will her affection for him not have been wasted, and he will not ruin another family's daughter.” Lady Wang replied, “What you say is naturally quite right, Master.” Jia Zheng had a maid from the room carry a message outside to Li Gui: “When Baoyu returns from school, let him finish his dinner before coming over. Tell him I still have questions to ask him.” Li Gui answered, “Yes.” When Baoyu returned from school and was just about to go and pay his respects, Li Gui said to him, “There is no need for you to go over just yet, Second Master. The Master has ordered you to come after dinner today. I hear he has something more to ask you.” To Baoyu, these words came like another muffled thunderclap. He had no choice but to pay his respects to Grandmother Jia and then return to the Garden for dinner. He swallowed the meal in a few hurried mouthfuls, quickly rinsed his mouth, and went over to Jia Zheng's quarters.

p.src: Jia Zheng was seated in his private study when Baoyu entered, paid his respects, and stood waiting at one side. Jia Zheng asked, “I have had matters weighing on my mind these past few days and forgot to ask you. The other day you said that after your tutor had taught you for a month, he would have you begin writing essays. It has now been nearly two months; have you begun or not?” Baoyu replied, “I have written only three so far. My tutor said there was no need to report it to you yet, sir, and that I should wait until my work had improved. That is why I have not dared mention it these past two days.” Jia Zheng asked, “What were the subjects?” Baoyu replied, “One was ‘At Fifteen I Set My Heart upon Learning,’ another was ‘Unresentful Though Unrecognized,’ and the third was the three characters ‘Then They Turn to Mo.’” Jia Zheng asked, “Do you have drafts of them all?” Baoyu replied, “I wrote them out in fair copy, and then my tutor corrected them.” Jia Zheng asked, “Did you bring them home, or are they still in the schoolroom?” Baoyu replied, “They are in the schoolroom.” Jia Zheng said, “Send someone to fetch them for me to see.” Baoyu hurriedly sent word to Beiming: “Have him go to the schoolroom. In my desk drawer there is a thin bamboo-paper notebook with the words ‘Class Exercises’ written on it. Tell him to bring it quickly.” Before long, Beiming brought it and handed it to Baoyu. Baoyu presented it to Jia Zheng. When Jia Zheng opened it, he saw that the first essay was entitled ‘At Fifteen I Set My Heart upon Learning.’ Baoyu’s original opening read: “The Sage set his heart upon learning, and had done so since childhood.” But Dai Ru had struck out the word “childhood” and explicitly substituted “fifteen.” Jia Zheng said, “Your original word ‘childhood’ fails to address the subject precisely. ‘Childhood’ covers the entire period from infancy until before the age of sixteen. In this chapter the Sage himself describes how his attainment in learning advanced with his years. Therefore fifteen, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, and seventy must all be stated explicitly, so that one sees at what age he reached one state and at what age he reached another. By changing your ‘childhood’ to ‘fifteen,’ your tutor made the meaning much clearer.” Coming to the amplification, he found that the deleted original read: “Not to set one’s heart upon learning is only natural for men.” Jia Zheng shook his head. “This is not merely childish; it shows that by nature you lack the aspirations of a scholar.” Then he read the next sentence, “Was it not difficult for the Sage to set his heart upon it at fifteen?” and said, “This makes even less sense.” He then read Dai Ru’s revision: “Who among men does not learn? Yet in the end, few set their hearts upon learning. Was this why the Sage spoke with such confidence of himself at the age of fifteen?” He asked, “Do you understand the correction?” Baoyu answered, “Yes, I understand.”

p.src: He next examined the second essay, entitled ‘Unresentful Though Unrecognized,’ and first read Dai Ru’s revision: “He who does not grow resentful at being unrecognized will never abandon the joy of what he advocates.” Then, narrowing his eyes at the deleted draft, he said, “And what is this of yours? —‘One able to keep resentment from the human heart is wholly a true scholar.’ The first sentence seems to treat only the three words ‘and is not resentful’ as the subject, while the next trespasses upon the distinction concerning the gentleman in the passage that follows. Only the corrected wording fits the precise scope of the subject. Moreover, the following sentence must clearly refer back to what precedes; only then does it accord with the meaning of the text. You must consider it with care.” Baoyu assented. Jia Zheng continued reading: “When one is not understood, there has scarcely ever been anyone who did not grow resentful, yet he was otherwise. If he did not derive joy from what he advocated, how could he have attained this?” The final sentence of the original had read: “Was he not a scholar of perfect purity?” Jia Zheng said, “This suffers from the same fault as the opening. The correction is passable. It is merely clear and can just about stand.” The third essay was ‘Then They Turn to Mo.’ After reading the title, Jia Zheng raised his head and pondered for a moment, then asked Baoyu, “Have your lessons reached this passage?” Baoyu replied, “My tutor said that Mencius was easier to understand, so he taught us Mencius first. We finished it only three days ago. We are now studying the first volume of the Analects.” Jia Zheng saw that the opening and amplification of this essay had scarcely been altered. The opening read: “It says that apart from forsaking Yang, there seems to be nowhere else to turn.” Jia Zheng said, “You have done remarkably well with the second sentence.” “Now Mo is not one to whom men desire to turn, yet Mo’s doctrines already possess half the realm. Apart from forsaking Yang, then, can one avoid turning to Mo?” Jia Zheng asked, “Did you write this yourself?” Baoyu answered, “Yes.” Jia Zheng nodded and said, “There is nothing particularly distinguished about it, but for a first attempt, it stays close enough to the point. The year before last, while I was in office, I too set the subject ‘Only a Gentleman Is Capable.’ Those young examination candidates had all read an earlier writer’s essay on it and, unable to devise ideas of their own, mostly resorted to copying. Have you read it?” Baoyu replied, “Yes, I have.” Jia Zheng said, “I want you to find a different approach. You may not echo the earlier writer. It will be enough if you compose only the opening.” Baoyu had no choice but to agree, and lowered his head to rack his barren brains. Jia Zheng clasped his hands behind his back and stood by the doorway, thinking as well. Just then a young page came darting out. On seeing Jia Zheng, he hurriedly stepped aside and stood still with his hands lowered. Jia Zheng asked, “What are you doing?” The page replied, “Her Ladyship’s sister has arrived at the Old Lady’s apartments. Second Mistress has sent word that the meal is to be prepared.” Jia Zheng heard him but said nothing. The page went on his way.

p.src: Now, ever since Baochai had moved back home, Baoyu had missed her terribly. When he heard that Aunt Xue had come, he assumed Baochai was with her and at once grew restless. Plucking up his courage, he replied, “I have composed an opening, though I do not know whether it is right.” Jia Zheng said, “Recite it for me.” Baoyu recited, “Not all beneath Heaven are scholars; those capable of living without property are few indeed.” Jia Zheng listened, nodded, and said, “That will do well enough. When writing essays hereafter, you must always distinguish the scope clearly and grasp the essential principle before putting brush to paper. Does the Old Lady know that you came here?” “Yes, she does,” said Baoyu. “In that case,” said Jia Zheng, “go back to the Old Lady.” Baoyu answered, “Yes,” and had no choice but to restrain himself and withdraw slowly. The moment he passed the screen beyond the moon gate of the covered passage, however, he flew like smoke all the way to the gate of the Old Lady's courtyard. Beiming hurried after him, calling anxiously, “Mind you don't fall! The Master is coming!” But Baoyu heard none of it. No sooner had he entered than he heard Lady Wang, Xifeng, Tanchun, and the others laughing and talking.

p.src: When the maids saw Baoyu, they hastily raised the curtain and whispered to him, “Your aunt is here.” Baoyu hurried inside to pay his respects to Aunt Xue, and only afterward went over to bid Grandmother Jia good evening. Grandmother Jia asked, “Why were you dismissed from school so late today?” Baoyu related in full how Jia Zheng had examined his essay and ordered him to compose an opening passage. Grandmother Jia's face beamed with delight. Baoyu then asked everyone, “Where is Cousin Bao sitting?” Aunt Xue laughed. “Your Cousin Bao did not come. She is at home sewing with Xiangling.” At this, Baoyu's spirits sank, though he could hardly leave at once. While they were still talking, the meal was served. Naturally, Grandmother Jia and Aunt Xue occupied the seats of honor, with Tanchun and the others seated beside them. “What about Baoyu?” asked Aunt Xue. Grandmother Jia said quickly with a smile, “Baoyu, sit here with me.” Baoyu hurriedly replied, “When school ended earlier, Li Gui brought Father's order that I was to go to him after eating. I quickly ordered a dish, poured tea over a bowl of rice, ate it, and went straight there. Please go ahead with your meal, Grandmother, Aunt, and cousins.” Grandmother Jia said, “In that case, Feng, come over and join me. Your aunt said just now that she is fasting today, so let the others eat by themselves.” Lady Wang also said, “Eat with the Old Lady and your aunt. There is no need to wait for me; I am fasting today.” Xifeng accordingly asked permission to join them. A maid set out a cup and chopsticks for her; Xifeng took up the winepot and poured a round for everyone before sitting down.

Grandmother Jia said, “In that case, Feng, come over and join me.
Your aunt said just now that she is fasting today, so let the others eat by themselves.”
Lady Wang also said, “Eat with the Old Lady and your aunt. There is no need to wait for me; I am fasting today.”
Xifeng accordingly asked permission to join them. A maid set out a cup and chopsticks for her; Xifeng took up the winepot and poured a round for everyone before sitting down.

p.src: They all drank together. Grandmother Jia then asked, “Aunt, when you mentioned Xiangling just now, I recalled hearing the maids speak of someone called ‘Qiuling’ the other day. I did not know who that was, but when I asked, I learned it was she. Why was the poor girl's perfectly good name changed?” Aunt Xue flushed scarlet and sighed. “Old Lady, please do not mention it. Ever since Pan married that unreasonable wife, there has been endless grumbling and quarreling every day, until ours hardly seems a proper household anymore. I have admonished her several times, but she is as stubborn as an ox and will not listen. I have not the strength to keep quarreling with them, so I can only let them do as they please. It was she who disliked the maid's name and had it changed.” Grandmother Jia said, “What possible importance can a name have?” Aunt Xue replied, “I am ashamed even to speak of it, though nothing that happens in our family is really unknown to you here. It was not truly because the name was bad. When she heard that Cousin Bao had given it to the girl, she deliberately set out to change it.” “And what is the reason for that?” asked Grandmother Jia. Aunt Xue kept wiping her tears with her handkerchief. Before she could speak, she sighed again and said, “You do not know, Old Lady, but nowadays my daughter-in-law deliberately picks quarrels with Cousin Bao. The other day, when you sent someone to inquire after me, our house was in the midst of an uproar.” Grandmother Jia quickly took up the conversation. “Was that when I heard the other day that your liver complaint was troubling you? I meant to send someone to see you, but later heard you had recovered, so no one was sent. If you ask me, Aunt, you should simply put the two of them out of your mind. Besides, they are newlyweds; after some time they will naturally settle down. To my mind, Cousin Bao has such a gentle and even-tempered nature that, young though she is, she surpasses her elders several times over. When that little maid returned the other day and told us about her, everyone here praised her for quite some time. A girl with Cousin Bao's generosity and disposition is truly one in a hundred. Forgive me for speaking boldly, but if such a girl became a family's daughter-in-law, how could her parents-in-law fail to cherish her, or anyone in the household, high or low, fail to respect her?” Baoyu had already grown weary of the conversation and was making an excuse to leave, but when he heard these words, he sat down again and listened on in a daze. Aunt Xue said, “That is no use. Good as she is, she is still only a girl. Having raised such a muddleheaded boy as Pan, I can never truly be at ease. I am always afraid that he will drink outside and land himself in trouble. Fortunately, the elder and younger young masters from your household are often with him, and that sets my mind somewhat at rest.” Hearing this, Baoyu broke in, “Aunt, you have even less cause to worry.

p.src: Just as the maids brought in the tea, Amber came over and whispered a few words in Grandmother Jia's ear. Grandmother Jia then said to Xifeng, “Hurry along and go see Qiaojie.” Xifeng did not yet know what had happened, and everyone else was taken aback as well. Amber then went over and told Xifeng, “Pinger has just sent a young maid to report to you, Second Mistress, that Qiaojie is not very well. She asks you to come quickly.” Grandmother Jia said, “Hurry along. Your aunt is no stranger to us.” Xifeng hastily assented and took her leave of Aunt Xue. Then Lady Wang said to her, “Go on ahead; I shall come shortly. A little child's soul is not yet firmly settled, so do not let the maids make a great commotion. Tell them to keep a careful eye on the cats and dogs in the room as well. However precious and blessed a child may be, these petty troubles will still arise.” Xifeng assented, then took a young maid with her and returned to her quarters.

p.src: Meanwhile, Aunt Xue asked once more about Daiyu's illness. Grandmother Jia replied, “That child Daiyu is well enough, except that she takes things too much to heart, and so her health is never very robust. In intelligence she is in no way inferior to Baochai; but when it comes to treating others with generosity, she cannot match her elder cousin Baochai's forbearance and unfailing readiness to yield.” After a little more casual conversation, Aunt Xue said, “You should rest now, Old Madam. I too must go home and have a look, since only Baochai and Xiangling are there. On my way, I shall go with her ladyship to see Qiaojie.” “Quite right,” said Grandmother Jia. As an older and more experienced person, you may be able to see what is wrong with her. If you tell them, they will have some idea what to do.” Aunt Xue then took her leave and went out with Lady Wang toward Xifeng's courtyard.

p.src: Now, after testing Baoyu, Jia Zheng was secretly pleased. He went outside and chatted with his retainers. When the conversation turned to what had just occurred, a recent arrival named Wang Ertiao, courtesy name Zuomei, who was an excellent player of Go, said, “In our opinion, Master Bao's learning has improved greatly.” “What improvement can there be?” replied Jia Zheng. “He merely understands a little. It is far too early to speak of ‘learning.’” Zhan Guang said, “That is merely your excessive modesty, venerable sir. Not only does Brother Wang say so; in our judgment too, Master Bao is certain to achieve high distinction.” Jia Zheng smiled. “That is only because you gentlemen are too fond of him.” Wang Ertiao spoke again. “There is one more matter which, at the risk of presumption, I should like to discuss with you, venerable sir.” “What is it?” asked Jia Zheng. Wang Ertiao smiled deferentially. “An acquaintance of mine, Lord Zhang, formerly Intendant of the Nan-Shao Circuit, has a daughter who is said to possess every virtue and accomplishment, as well as beauty and grace. She is not yet betrothed. He has no son, and his fortune is immense. But he will agree to the match only if the family possesses both wealth and rank and the prospective son-in-law is himself outstanding. During the two months I have been here, I have observed Master Bao's character and studies, and I am certain he is destined for great achievement. And with the standing of your venerable house, what objection could there be? If I go and speak to them, I guarantee that the match will be settled at once.” Jia Zheng said, “Baoyu is indeed old enough for marriage, and the Old Madam often speaks of the matter. But I have never known Lord Zhang very well.” Zhan Guang said, “I too know something of the Zhang family Brother Wang has mentioned. Moreover, they are old relatives of your elder brother's side of the family. You need only ask him to learn all about them.” Jia Zheng thought for a moment, then said, “I have never heard of any such relatives on my elder brother's side.” “So you did not know, venerable sir,” said Zhan Guang. “The Zhang household is actually related to the family of Uncle Xing.” Only then did Jia Zheng understand that they were relatives of Lady Xing. After sitting a while longer, he went inside, intending to tell Lady Wang and have her inquire of Lady Xing. But Lady Wang had accompanied Aunt Xue to Xifeng's quarters to see Qiaojie. It was already time to light the lamps when Aunt Xue departed and Lady Wang finally returned. Jia Zheng told her what Wang Ertiao and Zhan Guang had said, then asked what was wrong with Qiaojie. Lady Wang replied, “It seems she may be coming down with infantile convulsions.” “It is not too serious, is it?” asked Jia Zheng. “It looks as though convulsions may be coming on, but she has not actually had a seizure yet,” replied Lady Wang. Jia Zheng said no more. They retired separately, and nothing further need be said of that night.

p.src: The next day, Lady Xing came to pay her respects to Grandmother Jia. Lady Wang brought up the matter of the Zhang family, reporting it to Grandmother Jia while also questioning Lady Xing. Lady Xing said, “Although the Zhangs are old relatives, we have long been out of touch with them in recent years, so I do not know what their daughter is like. The other day, however, Madam Sun sent an old serving woman to inquire after us, and she happened to mention the Zhang family. She said they had a daughter and had asked the Suns to suggest the match if they knew of anyone suitable. I hear she is their only daughter and has been thoroughly pampered. She can read a little, but is unused to grand occasions and generally stays secluded in her room. Lord Zhang has also said that, as she is his only daughter, he will not marry her out of his household. He fears that strict parents-in-law might subject her to hardships she could not endure, and therefore insists that the bridegroom marry into their family and help him manage its affairs.” Before she had finished, Grandmother Jia broke in: “That is absolutely out of the question. Our Baoyu has never had enough people to wait on him as it is. How could he go and manage another family's household?” “That is exactly what I thought, Old Madam,” said Lady Xing. Grandmother Jia then said to Lady Wang, “When you return, tell your husband that these are my words: there can be no marriage with the Zhang family.” Lady Wang assented. Grandmother Jia then asked, “How was Qiaojie when you saw her yesterday? Earlier, Pinger came and told me that she was very poorly. I mean to go and see her myself.” Ladies Xing and Wang said, “Fond though you are of her, Old Madam, she could not bear the strain of receiving you there.” Grandmother Jia replied, “It is not only for her sake. I need to walk about a little myself and loosen up my limbs.” Then she instructed them, “Go and have your meal. When you return, come with me.” Ladies Xing and Wang assented, came out, and each went her own way.

p.src: When the meal was over, they all accompanied Grandmother Jia to Xifeng’s rooms. Xifeng hurried out to welcome them and ushered them inside. Grandmother Jia asked how Qiaojie was really doing. Xifeng replied, “I fear it may be the onset of convulsions.” Grandmother Jia said, “Then why haven’t you sent for someone at once to examine her?” “Someone has already gone to fetch the doctor,” said Xifeng. Grandmother Jia went into the room with Ladies Xing and Wang. They saw the nurse holding the child, wrapped in a little padded quilt of peach-pink satin; her face had turned bluish, and the ends of her brows and the wings of her nose twitched faintly. After looking at her, Grandmother Jia and Ladies Xing and Wang returned to sit in the outer room. While they were talking, a young maid came and reported to Xifeng, “Master Jia has sent someone to ask how the young miss is.” Xifeng said, “Tell Master Jia for me that we have sent for a doctor. Once he has written the prescription, I shall send word to him.” Grandmother Jia suddenly remembered the matter of the Zhang family and said to Lady Wang, “You should go and tell your husband at once, lest the other family make their proposal only to have him reject it afterward.” Then she asked Lady Xing, “Why have you stopped associating with the Zhang family?” Lady Xing replied, “Judging by the way the Zhang family conducts itself, it would be difficult for us to become related by marriage. They are far too miserly; such a match would only demean Baoyu.” Hearing this, Xifeng understood most of what was afoot and asked, “Are you ladies discussing Brother Baoyu’s marriage?” “Indeed we are,” said Lady Xing. Grandmother Jia then told Xifeng what had just been said. Xifeng laughed. “If I may be so bold as to say this before our Old Ancestress and the ladies: when a match made in Heaven is already before us, why look elsewhere?” Grandmother Jia asked with a smile, “Where is it?” Xifeng replied, “One is ‘Precious Jade’ and the other a ‘Golden Lock.’ How could you have forgotten, Old Lady?” Grandmother Jia smiled and said, “Your aunt was here yesterday. Why didn’t you mention it then?” Xifeng said, “With our Old Ancestress and the ladies present, how could there be any place for us youngsters to speak? Besides, Aunt came to visit our Old Ancestress. How could we raise such a matter then? It is for you ladies to go and make the proposal.” Grandmother Jia laughed, and Ladies Xing and Wang laughed as well. Grandmother Jia said, “It seems my wits truly are failing me.”

p.src: As they spoke, someone announced, “The doctor has arrived.” Grandmother Jia remained seated in the outer room, while Ladies Xing and Wang withdrew a little. The doctor entered with Jia Lian, paid his respects to Grandmother Jia, and then went into the inner room. After examining the child, he came out, stood below them, bowed, and reported to Grandmother Jia, “Half the little girl’s trouble comes from internal heat, and half from fright-induced convulsions. She must first be given a dose to disperse wind and phlegm, followed by Four-Spirits Powder, for the illness has come on severely. Most bezoar sold nowadays is counterfeit; only genuine bezoar will do.” Grandmother Jia thanked and dismissed him. The doctor went out with Jia Lian, wrote the prescription, and departed. Xifeng said, “We usually have ginseng in the house, but I doubt we have any bezoar. We can buy it outside, but it must be genuine.” Lady Wang said, “I shall send someone to your aunt’s house to look for some. Her son Pan has long done business with merchants from the western regions, so he may perhaps have some genuine bezoar. I’ll send someone to ask.” While they were speaking, all the young ladies came to see the child. After sitting for a while, they too left with Grandmother Jia and the others.

p.src: They decocted the medicine and poured it down Qiaojie’s throat. With a sudden cough, she vomited up both the medicine and the phlegm, and only then did Xifeng feel slightly relieved. Presently a young maid from Lady Wang’s quarters arrived with a tiny red-paper packet and said, “Second Mistress Lian, we have found some bezoar. Her Ladyship says you must personally make sure the weight is exact.” Xifeng acknowledged this and took the packet, then told Ping’er to add the full amounts of pearl, borneol, and cinnabar and quickly set it to decoct. She herself weighed it according to the prescription on a small steelyard and mixed it in, ready to give Qiaojie when she awoke. Just then Jia Huan lifted the curtain and came in, saying, “Second Sister, what is wrong with your Qiaojie? Mother sent me to see her.” Xifeng disliked the very sight of him and his mother. “She is a little better,” she said. Go back and tell your concubine-mother not to worry.” Jia Huan answered her, but continued peering about everywhere. After looking around for a while, he asked Xifeng, “I heard you have some bezoar here. I wonder what it looks like. Let me see it.” Xifeng said, “Stop making a nuisance of yourself here. The child has only just improved a little. The bezoar is already being decocted.” Hearing this, Jia Huan reached for the medicine pot to examine it. Before anyone could react, it tipped over with a hiss, and the spilled liquid extinguished half the fire. Realizing he had caused trouble and feeling embarrassed, Jia Huan hurriedly ran away. Xifeng was so furious she seemed to spit sparks. She cursed, “What mortal lifetime bred such a cursed enemy as you! Why must you come here and play such a spiteful trick? Your mother once tried to harm me, and now you have come to harm the child. Through how many lifetimes have you and I been enemies?” At the same time, she scolded Ping’er for failing to keep watch. While she was still railing, a maid came looking for Jia Huan. Xifeng said, “Go and tell Concubine Zhao that she has taken far too much trouble worrying about us. Qiaojie is certain to die now, so she need trouble herself no further!” Ping’er hurriedly prepared another batch of medicine and set it to decoct. Unable to make sense of the situation, the maid quietly asked her, “Why is Second Mistress Lian angry?” Ping’er told her how Brother Huan had knocked over the medicine pot. The maid said, “No wonder he dared not come back and has hidden himself somewhere else. There is no telling what will happen to Brother Huan tomorrow. Sister Ping, let me help you clean up.” “There is no need for that,” said Ping’er. Fortunately, a little bezoar was left. The medicine is ready now, so you may go.” The maid said, “I shall certainly tell Concubine Zhao when I return; that will stop her boasting every day.”

u.src: They decocted the medicine and poured it down Qiaojie’s throat. With a sudden cough, she vomited up both the medicine and the phlegm, and only then did Xifeng feel slightly relieved.
Presently a young maid from Lady Wang’s quarters arrived with a tiny red-paper packet and said, “Second Mistress Lian, we have found some bezoar.
Her Ladyship says you must personally make sure the weight is exact.”
Xifeng acknowledged this and took the packet, then told Ping’er to add the full amounts of pearl, borneol, and cinnabar and quickly set it to decoct.
She herself weighed it according to the prescription on a small steelyard and mixed it in, ready to give Qiaojie when she awoke.
Just then Jia Huan lifted the curtain and came in, saying, “Second Sister, what is wrong with your Qiaojie?
Mother sent me to see her.”
Xifeng disliked the very sight of him and his mother. “She is a little better,” she said.
Go back and tell your concubine-mother not to worry.”
Jia Huan answered her, but continued peering about everywhere.
After looking around for a while, he asked Xifeng, “I heard you have some bezoar here. I wonder what it looks like. Let me see it.”
Xifeng said, “Stop making a nuisance of yourself here. The child has only just improved a little.
The bezoar is already being decocted.”
Hearing this, Jia Huan reached for the medicine pot to examine it. Before anyone could react, it tipped over with a hiss, and the spilled liquid extinguished half the fire.
Realizing he had caused trouble and feeling embarrassed, Jia Huan hurriedly ran away.
Xifeng was so furious she seemed to spit sparks. She cursed, “What mortal lifetime bred such a cursed enemy as you!
Why must you come here and play such a spiteful trick?
Your mother once tried to harm me, and now you have come to harm the child.
Through how many lifetimes have you and I been enemies?”
At the same time, she scolded Ping’er for failing to keep watch.
While she was still railing, a maid came looking for Jia Huan.
Xifeng said, “Go and tell Concubine Zhao that she has taken far too much trouble worrying about us.
Qiaojie is certain to die now, so she need trouble herself no further!”
Ping’er hurriedly prepared another batch of medicine and set it to decoct. Unable to make sense of the situation, the maid quietly asked her, “Why is Second Mistress Lian angry?”
Ping’er told her how Brother Huan had knocked over the medicine pot.
The maid said, “No wonder he dared not come back and has hidden himself somewhere else.
There is no telling what will happen to Brother Huan tomorrow.
Sister Ping, let me help you clean up.”
“There is no need for that,” said Ping’er.
Fortunately, a little bezoar was left. The medicine is ready now, so you may go.”
The maid said, “I shall certainly tell Concubine Zhao when I return; that will stop her boasting every day.”

p.src: The maid went back and, sure enough, told Concubine Zhao what had happened. Concubine Zhao cried angrily, “Go and fetch Huan at once!” Huan had been hiding in the outer room, but a maid found him and brought him in. Concubine Zhao immediately began to berate him: “You wretched little beast! Why did you spill her medicine and bring her curses down on us? I only told you to go and ask after her; there was no need to enter. But you insisted on going in, and instead of leaving at once, you had to go looking for lice on a tiger’s head. Just wait until I report this to the master—you’ll see whether he has you beaten!” While Concubine Zhao was still speaking, Jia Huan could be heard in the outer room saying things even more shocking and horrifying. What he said remains unknown; the next chapter will reveal it.
